name: room
text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Add a **large, high-contrast skip link** at the top of every page, visible by default. This ensures keyboard users can bypass repetitive navigation blocks in one click, solving the core keyboard navigation problem without relying on hidden elements that may fail in some browsers. The trade-off is a small permanent UI element, but it’s a standard pattern (like on gov.uk) that improves usability for everyone, not just assistive tech users.

name: Reader
text: A large, high-contrast skip link risks pushing primary content below the fold on small screens, making it harder for *all* users—not just keyboard users—to reach key information quickly. Instead, use a compact skip link that only appears on keyboard focus, paired with a visible focus indicator to avoid confusion for first-time users. Settle this by testing with real screen-reader users on mobile and desktop—if the skip link delays access or obscures content, revert to the compact version.
